title: Eurogate/Eurokai Q3 2026 interim report: 9M throughput up 8.7% to 11.35m TEU, record quarter
summary: EUROKAI (50% owner of the EUROGATE JV) published its Q3 2026 interim report on 11 November 2026: group container terminals handled 11,346,104 TEU in Jan-Sep 2026 (+8.7%), with Hamburg 1.80m TEU (+3.1%), Bremerhaven 3.91m (+6.0%), Wilhelmshaven 1.34m (+24.2%), Tangier 2.38m (+5.0%), Limassol 0.38m (+4.0%), Contship Italia 1.34m (+4.1%) and the new Damietta terminal 187,600 TEU (operations started Feb 2026, still loss-making). Trade press (Hansa) reported a record Q3 of 3.93m TEU (+9.4%). Outlook: 2026 consolidated earnings above prior year thanks to ~EUR 20m from the NTB Bremerhaven partnership extension with APM Terminals (EUR 1bn modernisation, 3m to 4m TEU, completion expected Q4 2026); the 20% CMA Terminals and 20% Hanseatic Global Terminals (Hapag-Lloyd) stakes in Eurogate Hamburg still await binding approvals, now expected H1 2027. Strong North Range volume growth at a direct DP World competitor in Europe, led by Wilhelmshaven (Gemini hub).

title: CMA CGM breaks ground on EUR 40m extension of Lyon Rhône Terminal inland multimodal hub
summary: CMA CGM laid the first stone on 12 November 2026 for the modernisation and extension of Lyon Rhône Terminal at the Port Édouard-Herriot (Lyon), which CMA Terminals has operated since April 2025 under a 30-year sub-concession from Compagnie Nationale du Rhône. The c. EUR 40m (about USD 46m at ~1.16 USD/EUR) programme adds a 3-hectare platform extension, two extra rail sidings (seven in total), renovated roads/buildings and digitalised operations, lifting annual capacity from c. 120,000 TEU to 200,000 TEU by 2032; works run 2026-2028. Project company shareholders are CMA Terminals Holding (67%), Banque des Territoires (25%) and the Lyon and Aix-Marseille chambers of commerce (4% each). It deepens CMA CGM's hinterland network linking Fos-sur-Mer to the Rhône-Saône corridor and rail links to Calais, Dunkirk, Bettembourg and Piacenza, an inland-logistics play comparable to DP World's European intermodal footprint.

title: MSC-controlled HHLA 9M 2026 results: Hamburg throughput down 7.7%, EBIT -31%, guidance cut
summary: Hamburger Hafen und Logistik AG (HHLA), controlled by MSC via Port of Hamburg Beteiligungsgesellschaft (MSC 49.9%, City of Hamburg 50.1%; minority squeeze-out completed in 2026), reported 9M 2026 results on 12 November 2026: container throughput fell 7.3% to 4.45m TEU (Hamburg terminals -7.7% to 4.20m TEU on automation ramp-up, shifting cargo flows, winter weather and Q3 strikes; Odesa terminal nearly idle in Q3), group revenue +3.3% to EUR 1,375m, EBIT -30.7% to EUR 81.2m and net profit down 94% to EUR 2m after EUR 21.4m impairments (HHLA Sky sold end-October, omoqo closed). 2026 guidance was cut to group EBIT EUR 115-135m (from 150-170m) and capex EUR 380-430m. Intermodal (METRANS) grew with rail volume +0.6% and EBIT +2.3%. Signals that MSC's flagship German terminal asset is losing share to Eurogate in Hamburg while MSC builds its wider TiL terminal network.

title: CMA CGM Q3 2026 results: group EBITDA up 61.6% to USD 4.78bn; CEVA Logistics revenue up 19% but EBITDA down 14%
summary: CMA CGM reported Q3 2026 revenue of USD 18.40bn (+31.1% y/y), EBITDA of USD 4.78bn (+61.6%, 25.9% margin) and group net income of USD 2.32bn, on 6.51m TEU carried (+5.5%). The logistics arm CEVA Logistics posted revenue of USD 5.46bn (+19.2%, boosted by the FedEx Supply Chain acquisition completed in the quarter) but EBITDA fell 14.4% to USD 366m (6.7% margin) on weak freight forwarding and automotive markets; CEVA is simplifying its organisation under Patrick Moebel. 'Other activities' (incl. terminals) grew revenue 27.1% to USD 1.51bn with EBITDA of USD 413m. The group highlighted CMA Terminals' 49% stake in Nador Container Terminal (Morocco) and the Jeddah Terminal 4 development with Red Sea Gateway Terminal, confirming continued terminal and logistics expansion into DP World's core Red Sea/Mediterranean markets.

title: CMA CGM launches EUR 400m senior unsecured notes offering
summary: CMA CGM S.A. issued a pre-stabilisation notice on 17 November 2026 for a EUR 400m (about USD 465m at ~1.16 USD/EUR) senior unsecured notes issue, with BNP Paribas as stabilisation coordinator alongside CACIB, HSBC, Société Générale, UniCredit, BofA, CIC, ING and Santander; the stabilisation period runs from 17 November to no later than 24 December 2026. Maturity, coupon and use of proceeds were not stated in the notice. The deal follows record Q3 2026 earnings and extends the group's funding capacity for its terminal, logistics (CEVA) and fleet investment programme.
